tasting_notes: Dried apricot, cocoa, coffee, and spice notes highlight this excellent entry-level blend. Reduced with water very slightly to 48% ABV, its pure flavors have excellent staying power on the palate. A blend of folle blanche, colombard, and ugni blanc, between 5 and 10 years old.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength; Cépages Nobles
tasting_notes: A cask strength 1972 vintage armagnac from traditional producer Domaine Boingneres, who use a high proportion of the seldom-seen Folle Blanche grape in their assemblage.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength; Cépages Nobles
Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength; Cépages Nobles
tasting_notes: A nose of vanilla custard and maple syrup transitions to a palate of leather and tobacco leaf. A whisper of banana pudding gives way to lemon oil and a hint of copper on the finish. Distilled in 1985 on a gas-fueled copper alambic Armagnacais column still; cépages approximately one-third each of Ugni Blanc, Colombard, and Folle Blanche.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength; Ugni Blanc
Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength; Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: Light copper, with a complex floral bouquet of rose and almond blossom along with aromas of fig and candied orange that roll onto the palate, developing seamlessly into gingerbread on the midpalate and finishing fresh with notes of mint and licorice. Pretty, delicate, yet still dense and intense.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength; Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: Deep amber color. Dried orange fruits on the nose, along with some coffee and chocolate cream notes. The palate is fine and seamless; spice notes ride along the fruit rich in glycerin, and the flavors, rich in alcohol and oak, stay on the palate for several minutes.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength; Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: Deep amber. Vanilla scented oak, mocha, and spice on the nose. Toffee, creamy orange and even more spice on the palate. The finish is flavorful, round, and long.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Single Cask, Cask Strength; Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: Amber. Floral aromas, along with mocha and vanilla on the nose; on the palate, dried fruit (apricot, orange) glide across the palate, with a burst of alcohol and spice on the finish. The finish is long. This young, unadulterated armagnac is pure, intense, and explosive. A combination of two folle blanche barrels from 2007, 500 bottles bottled at cask strength without filtration.

A nose of spice and blonde caramel, with nuances of quince paste, toast and cinnamon. On the palate, peppery orange zest evolves into even more caramel alongside roasted apples. A finish of chocolate and liquorice. Aged 3 to 5 years.

A deep amber colour. A lively nose, both ripe and floral which gives off an almost minty freshness. The attack is round, and its intensity increases with notes of oaky spices with hints of fresh mint. The finish is enriched with nuances of liquorice and macerated fruit. Aged 5 to 7 years.

An amber colour. A heady nose of dried fruits and quince paste alongside notes of dried flowers. As it airs, nuances of coconut begin to develop. The attack is fleshy and honeyed. On the palate, a beautiful mix of fruit and oak which opens to accents of prunes, almonds and rancio. The lengthy finish is slightly toasted with a subtle hint of leather. Average age of 15 years.

A deep colour with amber highlights. A nose that evokes orange zest, sweet cocoa, and toasted almond. A harmonious and fluid palate with complex aromas of fruit, rancio, and liquorice. Phenomenal length combined with a luxurious texture finishing with notes of spices, nutmeg, and ginger. At least 20 years of ageing.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Hors d'Âge, Blend; Le Légendaire
tasting_notes: A delicate golden hue. A nose of Tarte Tatin and orange blossom which, when given some air, takes on notes of toffee. The attack is fresh, supple, and nervous with flavours of blonde caramel and liquorice. The palate blossoms with intense and dynamic notes of roasted fruit, orange zest and exotic spices (nutmeg, grey pepper, cinnamon). A wonderfully smooth finish. Hors d'Âge, average age of 15 years.

Its bright colour is tinted gold and orange. The nose reveals buttery notes, mirabelle plums and roasted pineapple. On the palate, one will find notes of coffee, toast, and cayenne pepper. Aged minimum 10 years.

A golden colour with copper highlights. A nose with notes of orange peel and spices. On the palate, hints of bitter cocoa and liquorice and a surprising, almost oily texture. Great power and great length. Aged 18 years minimum.

The colour is golden with orange highlights. The nose is reminiscent of white pepper and ginger. The palate is marked by bitter orange, banana, and spices. The finish gives way to candied fruit notes. Aged a minimum 20 years.

Aromas of pear and linden blossom lead to notes of iodine, almond and blond caramel upon aeration. A fresh mouthfeel with melon and violets blends seamlessly into the intensity of black pepper. The lengthy finish of spices mingles with flavours of plum and green apple. A finish of dried flowers and fresh spices. Aged for a few months in stainless steel tanks; vintage-dated; 50cl bottle.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; VS, Folle Blanche; Pure Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: A pale golden hue. A delicate nose of sweet toffee, tarte Tatin and almond paste. Scents of currants and fine wood appear as the Armagnac breathes. The initial freshness and supple texture of the eau-de-vie finish in a delicate harmony of toffee and spices. A blend of different vintages; aged 3 to 5 years.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Folle Blanche, Cask Strength; Pure Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: A golden hue. A sappy, vanilla nose alongside plum and citrus. Intense and powerful, the palate is tense, marked with vegetal and fruity nuances and cocoa notes. Beautiful length on the palate that leads to a finish of orange zest. Minimum ageing 8 years, cask strength.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Folle Blanche, Cask Strength; Pure Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: A deep golden colour. A nose replete with fresh fruit (orange, lemon, apple) and flowers. On the palate, the initial freshness intensifies with notes of candied pineapple, nutmeg, white pepper and citrus zest. On the finish, a subtle hint of liquorice coats the fruit and spice, finishing with a hint of walnut (rancio). Minimum ageing 12 years, cask strength.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Folle Blanche, Cask Strength; Pure Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: A brilliant colour with mahogany highlights. The nose is intense and complex with candied orange, rancio, honey and Madagascar pepper. The attack is both generous and intense. While the palate is powerful, it is not aggressive, but rather mouth coating and shows exotic spice notes. The finish reveals the brightness of the rancio in combination with sweeter flavours of dried fruit, pineapple, apple and grape. Voted Best Spirit of the Year / Supreme Champion Spirit 2022 at the International Spirits Challenge. Minimum ageing 15 years, cask strength.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Folle Blanche, Cask Strength; Pure Folle Blanche
tasting_notes: A golden robe with orange highlights. A nose that evokes aromas of caramel and fresh pastry. The palate is fluid, powerful and fresh, offering great persistence of spice, stone fruits, exotic fruits, and honeysuckle sensations. An incredibly long and intense finish of stone fruits, dried fruits and spices. Minimum ageing 25 years, cask strength.

A golden colour with orange highlights. A nose of orange blossom, roasted pineapple, notes of cooked apples and nutmeg. As it breathes, bursts of cardamom flowers arise from the glass. The palate is delicate and honeyed with sappy nuances and flavours of macerated stone fruits. The finish adds a touch of Sichuan pepper. Bottled at cask strength.

A beautiful acacia honey colour. Sap and warmth on the nose blend notes of toast and subtle nuances of roasted pineapple and flambeed banana. A dense, oily, and powerful palate enhanced with spice (Cayenne pepper) that lingers with nuances of cocoa, sap, liquorice and bark. Bottled at cask strength.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Hors d'Âge, Cask Strength, Blend; Montreur d'Ours
mash_bill: Plant de Graisse 70%, Ugni Blanc & Baco 30%
tasting_notes: An elegant and suave nose evokes orange peels and flowers with a background of spices. The palate shows a unique smoothness, typical of Plant de Graisse, both dense and supple. Spice and chocolate notes, a hint of candied orange and pear, giving way to a phenomenally lengthy finish with hints of liquorice and dried fruits. Aged between 10 and 20 years depending on the barrels.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Cask Strength, Blend; L'Armagnac du Centenaire
mash_bill: Ugni Blanc, Baco, Folle Blanche, Plant de Graisse
tasting_notes: A uniquely floral and fruity Bas-Armagnac. Ugni blanc brings freshness and finesse; Baco power and structure; Folle Blanche elegance with floral and spicy fragrances; Plant de Graisse a touch of richness and roundness. Will leave a deep impression of harmony with a long and sensual finish. Ageing of 10 to 30 years depending on each barrel, cask strength; the precise blend remains a family secret.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Hors d'Âge, Blend; L'Armagnac Cabine
tasting_notes: Copper coloured with golden red highlights. A subtle nose of honey and dried apricot. On the palate, hints of vine peach and plum mingle with surprising touches of graphite. The finish, of exceptional persistence, blossoms with notes of candied fruit and cocoa accompanied by touches of spices and ginger. Aged 20 to 30 years.
Golden color; fruity nose, mellow on the mouth; for cocktails or on the rocks
Amber color; fruity nose with light pepper, coconut and walnut, honey and glazed plum finish; subtle and balanced on the palate
Light coppery; powerful warm nose of fruits and spices; full palate of glazed ripe plums, toasted oak, nutmeg, hints of rancio, long smooth finish

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Hors d'Âge; Réserve de la Famille

tasting_notes: Old gold; elegant nose of dried herbs and sweet spices, complex; complex, bitter, elegant, long palate (min. 60 years in oak before glass dame-jeanne)
Dried apricots, honeysuckle and baking spices (bottled January 2020)
Leather, vanilla and dried fruit on the nose; sweet baking spices, toasted oak, apricots, vanilla and dried fruit on the palate
Matured in French oak casks until bottling January 2020
Rich and full bodied with notes of violets and stone fruits
Aged in oak for a minimum of two years. Versatile in nature, can be used in cocktail, over ice or neat.

Aged for a minimum of 5 years. Nose very open, rich and pleasant: quince, caramel, peanut aromas, menthol note, toasted bread, soft spices. Palate round attack but powerful in alcohol, fresh, light bitterness with toasted brioche aromas.
A fruit driven, but spicy flavoured Armagnac. The flavours are complex and mouthfilling.
Offers up some complex and spicy flavours whilst being suitably easy to drink. Great after a meal.
A special edition Armagnac that far exceeds the required age for an XO. The brandies used are aged between 25 and 45 years.
A perfectly aged Armagnac with rich spicy flavours of prune, oak, leather and cinnamon.

Very intense amber colour with olive green reflections. Very aromatic nose offers spice scents and rancio notes (nuts, butter); aromas found again in the mouth, very balanced. Elegant on the nose with peppery and spicy notes; complexity of cocoa and spice in the mouth.
An incredible Armagnac from the 1934 harvest. Bottled in 2013 after nearly eighty years.
Distilled from grapes that were harvested in 1940 as the German army marched across Europe.
An old vintage Armagnac from the 1941 harvest.
A stunning Armagnac that was distilled in 1968. Flavours of citrus and plum work alongside sweet vanilla and caramel notes.

Pale yellow colour, bright and clear. Nose light note of wood and vanilla (ageing in barrels). Mouth clean and lively, well balanced; notes of vanilla, fresh grapes and apples; fresh-fruit finish of great length.

Golden coloured Armagnac, bright and clear. Nose aromas of prunes, vanilla and fresh grapes. Mouth striking and clean attack followed by notes of quince, tannins, prunes; supple and round finish with light vanilla and great fullness.

mash_bill: Ugni Blanc 70%, Baco 20%, Colombard 5%, Folle Blanche 5%
tasting_notes: Minimum 6 years old. Flavors of cocoa, orange rind, cake batter and vanilla; soft tannins on the finish and a touch of rancio. Roasted chestnut, baked pear, pineapple, caramel, black raisins, prunes and old oak; creamy textured, semisweet entry, nutty/woody midpalate, oily oaky finish.

mash_bill: Ugni Blanc 70%, Baco 20%, Colombard 5%, Folle Blanche 5%
tasting_notes: Bears an age statement of 12 years. Amber colour, bright and clear. Nose rancio, nuts, vanilla, toasted notes, mellow wood. Mouth clean attack, soft with light tannins; note of rancio with a round and supple finish of great length.
Minimum 4 years old. Blend of young eaux-de-vie selected for their fruit and softness. Aromas of plum, pear, finish on sweet almond.
Minimum 6 years old. Blend of eaux-de-vie with prolonged oak ageing for complexity. Fruit notes of young vintages married with spicy notes of reserve vintages; fresh, gourmand profile.
Minimum 12 years old. Signature of the Dartigalongue style. Notes of candied fruit (pineapple, orange), toasted oak, spices and sandalwood. Powerful, controlled palate with remarkable length.
Minimum 20 years old. The age of perfect harmony, roundness, balance. Silky mouth texture. Very rich bouquet with notes of gingerbread, liquorice and candied ginger.

Minimum 30 years old. The quintessence of the Dartigalongue style, from an exceptionally long oak ageing. Ode to noble rancio, with typical aromas of walnut, dried fruits and smoked wood. Incredible complexity.
Unaged. Nose subtle notes of pear, apple and white flowers. Palate very ample, unctuous texture, finish on sweet almond.

barrel_type: One pass in red oak casks
tasting_notes: One pass in red oak casks. Nose delicate notes of vanilla, plum and peach. Palate very intense and straight, finish marked by spices.

barrel_type: Two passes in new oak casks
tasting_notes: Two passes in new oak casks. Aromas of toasted bread, cocoa, roasting, spices highlighting the influence of Gascon oak.

Created for the 180th anniversary of the house. Blend at 42% of 5 vintages: 1979, 1983, 1986, 1992 and 1994, selected for quality and complementarity. Remarkable for its finesse, gourmandise and length on the palate.
Frank nose of medium-toast light wood giving a woody, discreet, blonde note; fresh on the palate, revealing all the youthfulness of this already well-balanced armagnac.
Golden colour, already-evolved woody nose, pronounced vanilla flavour with floral notes; easy on the palate with a gentle vanilla and spice attack, then the wood returns to linger.

Amber tending towards dark brown; mild nose dominated by wood of the mature rancio kind; soft and caressing on the palate where the alcohol disappears, leaving heightened notes of wood, rancio, cocoa, chocolate.

spirit_name: Domaine de Joÿ À un moment donné
special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Folle Blanche; À un moment donné
tasting_notes: Vanilla-heavy, fruity nose where alcohol is not in evidence; already very supple and unctuous on the palate, where vanilla and toasty notes reign.
A frank nose of medium-toast light wood gives a woody, discreet, blonde note; fresh on the palate, revealing all the youthfulness of this already well-balanced armagnac.
Golden colour, already-evolved woody nose, pronounced vanilla flavour with floral notes; gentle on the palate with a gentle vanilla and spice attack, then wood returns to linger.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; XO; Baco; Armagnac by Joÿ XO Premium
tasting_notes: Shiny amber colour with dark brown reflections; spicy cinnamon nose with notes of cocoa, candied orange and toasted hazelnuts; ample, unctuous and fluid on the palate, dominated by rancio and candied fruit; finish fresh and slightly mentholated.

spirit_name: Domaine d'Espérance VS 5 fûts - brut de fûts
special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; VS; Cask Strength; 5 fûts - brut de fûts
tasting_notes: Blend of 2 grape varieties from 5 different casks at still proof, no reduction; as an apéritif with ice cubes or within a fruit- or coffee-based cocktail.
Blend of 3, 4 or 5 complementary vintages aged at least 5 years; easy to drink, revealing fruity aromas backed by oak flavours.
Blend of at least 4 vintages, youngest aged at least 10 years; beautiful copper colour, wide range of aromas (prune, orange, vanilla) and great complexity in the mouth.
Blend of at least 4 vintages, youngest aged at least 18 years; beautiful copper colour, wide range of aromas (prune, orange, vanilla) and great complexity.
Blend of 4 or 5 armagnacs aged in oak casks for more than 20 years.

Single assembly blending the first 30 years at Espérance from 49 barrels of Folle Blanche and Baco (1990-2020); nose of orange typical of Espérance, vivacity of the young armagnacs with the fat of the 1990s Baco and floral notes of the 2000s Folle Blanche. Available only in magnum.

White armagnac with no oak ageing; blend of Folle Blanche and Baco distilled at low degree to preserve grape aromas; drunk like a fruit brandy or chilled like vodka, a must for cocktails, pairs with smoked salmon, eel and cold cuts.

spirit_name: Château de Lacquy Carafe des Siècles
special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Hors d'Âge; Blend; Carafe des Siècles
tasting_notes: Unique blend of armagnacs distilled between 1800 and 1980, brut de fût; characterised by great finesse and voluptuousness; floral aromas with hints of spice, vanilla, cocoa and candied fruit; exceptional length.

tasting_notes: A rich, oaky Hors d'Age Armagnac matured for at least 10 years. Notes of oak spice, prunes and orange blossom fill the palate.

A fruity, rich XO Armagnac matured for at least 15 years in Landais oak casks. The palate offers notes of tobacco, dried fruits and cinnamon, with hints of chestnut, honey and orange blossom lingering in the finish.
An unaged Armagnac eau-de-vie with subtle floral character and pungent fruity notes of pears, plums, and grapes.

Dark amber with deep golden highlights. Round, creamy notes emit aromas of plum, vanilla, toffee, and spice. Great balance on the soft palate, with additional notes of walnut, pepper and a touch of smoke. The flavors linger on the palate for over a minute.

Dark amber with deep golden highlights. Rich nose shows notes of dried plums, leather, vanilla and spice. Palate is round and soft, with mouth-coating flavors that include cocoa, almonds and oak. Finishes long.
Dried fruit (prune, quince), leather, smoked honey, walnut, and spice. Soft and long.
Robe: ambrée avec reflets acajou. Nez: souple avec des notes d'agrumes, oranges confites et pointe de cèdre. Bouche: attaque souple en bouche, notes de vanille et belle longueur.
Rich texture emits liquered apricot, cherry, and plum. Lots of fruit on the palate, with a long finish that shows additional notes of orange peel, almond, and spice.
Robe: tabac avec reflets orangés. Nez: souple avec des notes réglissées, légèrement poivrées. Bouche: attaque souple, rapidement suivie d'une agréable fougue, finale longue et subtilement réglissée.

spirit_name: Château de Ravignan Bas-Armagnac Folle Blanche 2003

tasting_notes: Robe: dorée aux reflets orange. Nez: abricot frais et reine-claude. Bouche: frais et ample, abricot et cannelle.

Nez: le nez est fin et élégant, tout d'abord sur des arômes de fruits compotés puis surviennent les notes d'abricot confit. Bouche: l'attaque en bouche est franche et intense, sur des notes de pain grillé et d'épices (girofle). Finale: la finale sur des notes de rancio est très persistante.

Nose: a first slightly wooded nose carried on the compoted fruit. Mouth: the attack is frank, alcohol subtly reveals aromas of cooked prunes. Final: a lightness final. Aromas of undergrowth and fern delivering rancio flavors of smoked tea.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Cask Strength; Baco; Single Cask; Millésime

mash_bill: Baco / Ugni Blanc / Folle Blanche / Colombard
tasting_notes: Intense aromas of ripe fruit, plums and sweet pastries; subtle and smooth on the palate with hints of vanilla and citrus and a long aftertaste. Aged 6-12 years.

Deep-amber color; intense bouquet of prunes, vanilla, cinnamon, cocoa, coffee, almonds and toast with hints of orange peel and dried apricot; soft, velvety mouthfeel and a remarkably long aftertaste. Aged 15-25 years.

Deep-amber blend of over 30 eaux-de-vie, majority Baco; bouquet of candied fruit, spice and vanilla; powerful and rich on the palate with persistent rancio typical of old Bas Armagnacs. Aged 12-20 years.
Blend of the most remarkable 420L casks aged 21-25 years; created for premium whisky enthusiasts and singular armagnac aficionados.

Mahogany-colored blend of nearly 40 eaux-de-vie, almost 50% Baco; very complex bouquet of prune, candied fruit and cocoa; subtle hints of hazelnut and ripe fruit with oaky notes. Aged 20-30 years; named 'World's Best Brandy' in San Francisco.
Unaged eau-de-vie blended exclusively from Folle Blanche; intensely aromatic, fresh and fruity; round and well-balanced on the palate with a soft aftertaste.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime; Cask Strength; Single Cask
tasting_notes: Deep mahogany with coppery reflections; nose of rancio, dried fruits, candied fig and walnut with sweet spices, orange peel and subtle lactic and lightly smoked notes; long, warm finish of dried fruits and spices. Bottled at natural cask strength.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime; Cask Strength; Single Cask
tasting_notes: Light mahogany; nose of rancio, dried fruits, figs, nuts, spices, orange bark, milky and smoked notes; great maturity, power and deep complexity on the palate. Bottled at natural cask strength.

Aged for a minimum of six years, but containing some much older eaux-de-vie.
Plenty of dried fruit, oaky spice, and a rancio notes developing.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Single Cask; Cask Strength; Millésime

tasting_notes: This complex, balanced VSOP Armagnac won a Silver Medal at the International Spirit Challenge in London 2004. This was aged for 6 months in new oak before 7 years in old oak.

spirit_name: Baron de Sigognac 50 Year Old Decanter
Baron de Sigognac 70 Ans d'Age Heritage

tasting_notes: Aroma: Dried tropical fruits and candied orange with chocolate, linseed and fruitcake. Taste: Dried fruit, tropical fruit and linseed oil rubbed leather with cinnamon spice and grated ginger. Aftertaste: Spicy orange zest and chocolate with lingering nuts and raisins.
Assemblage of Armagnac aged 5 to 7 years, reduced to 42%; menthol and licorice notes, smooth and round.
Assemblage of Armagnac aged 10 years, reduced to 42%; fresh menthol and eucalyptus, prune on the palate and a smoky finish.
Assemblage of Armagnac aged 12 to 15 years, reduced to 42%; prunes, dried fruits, vanilla and coconut; melted, silky tannins.
Distilled 1995, aged 23 years in barrels, reduced to 42%; spiced brioche, smooth with hints of rancio and almonds.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength, Single Cask; Brut de Fût
tasting_notes: Distilled 1996, aged 21 years in barrels at 54.6%; rancio on walnuts and Tonka bean aromas.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength, Single Cask; Brut de Fût
tasting_notes: Distilled 2006, aged 11 years in barrels at 50.1%; minty freshness, round attack, slightly vanillaed mouth with lemon verbena.
Amber dress; spicy aromas of cinnamon and pear with a touch of white figs.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Reduced Strength; Carafe 20 ans d'âge
tasting_notes: 50cl carafe at 42%; youngest eau-de-vie aged 20 years; amber, cinnamon and pear with white fig; greengage plum, creme brulee, vanilla finish.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Hors d'Âge; Vie de Plaisir
tasting_notes: Assemblage of Armagnacs aged 12 to 15 years, reduced to 42%; prunes and dried fruits with slight vanilla and coconut; melted silky tannins.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; Millésime, Cask Strength, Single Cask; Collection 2000

tasting_notes: A very soft, fruity Armagnac, well balanced; bright amber; nose of fruit and spice (plum, vanilla, walnut); round, fresh texture with woody, spicy notes.
Amber, bright and limpid; nose of cooked prunes with vanilla and spices such as cinnamon; frank attack, very light wood note; finish on prunes and rancio.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; VSOP, Single Cask, Cask Strength; Double Cask Brut de Fût
tasting_notes: Blend of two rich, complex vintages bottled cask strength without filtration at 50.04% vol; amber and bright; nose of fruit and spice on a caramelised, mocha-dominant base; round, fresh texture with woody, spicy and caramel notes.

special_designation: Bas-Armagnac; XO, Single Cask, Cask Strength; XO Single Cask Brut de Fût
tasting_notes: Over 18 years old, finished 5 years in a Gascon pedunculate oak barrel; bottled cask strength unfiltered at 47.9% vol; pale topaz; rich floral and fruity nose, honeysuckle, red and exotic fruits, grilled wood notes; warm, round, balanced palate on red fruit with a fresh passion-fruit finish.

Complex nose mixing pear and lightly stewed banana; round, powerful palate with a fireworks of orchard-fruit and floral flavours, soft brioche and honeyed finish; serve chilled or frozen, neat or in cocktails.
Sustained amber colour; supple nose marked by candied plum evolving towards prune; rather fat palate with a typical rancio for this length of ageing and light almond notes.

tasting_notes: A blend of 6 years and more, aged in oak barrels, tamed by the more mature 12 year old brandies in the blend; complex nose and powerful palate; aromas of ripe fruit, vanilla and gentle spice with notes of baked apple, caramel and light oak.

At over five decades, this Armagnac is a kaleidoscope of rancio, pimento, five-spice, anise candy, and preserved fig. The alcohol has broken down completely to a warm, glycerol tide softly washing the dark flavors across the palate. The finish continues to reverberate the earlier flavors and lasts and lasts.

Deep, brown pitch with no caramel coloring. The nose follows with a deep, nutty profile. At 29 years old there is a youthful spike of acidity that adds nice structure to the more autumnal flavors. At only 44.7% alcohol the finish is rich without leaving much burn.

special_designation: Armagnac-Ténarèze; Millésime, Single Cask, Cask Strength
tasting_notes: A very nice amber tint with green sheens. Limpid and lustrous. A strongly intense entry and finish. Complex and generous aromas revealing notes of candied fruit, stones, prunes, figs, walnuts. A structured finish that lasts with a beautiful elegance.

special_designation: Armagnac-Ténarèze; Millésime, Single Cask, Cask Strength
tasting_notes: Nose slightly acidic and sour with notes of vinegar, sour white grape juice, apple cider, citrus and grilled fish. Palate closer to wine, with herbs such as thyme or oregano, lemon and apple. Finish rather short with apples, cider, apple vinegar and grapefruit.

Nose of roasted chestnut, caramelized almonds with a pinch of salt, oak, pomace, multi-grain bread, chocolate and roasted coffee. Palate full proof but lean, with bread, leather, dried fruits and dry red wine. Finish medium-long with wood, spices and juniper berries.

Nose of leather, rum-soaked raisins, oak, dried apricot and mild nuts, later more rancid and buttery notes. Palate thin, woody and somewhat bitter with stale black tea, walnuts, chestnuts and wood. Finish long and bitter.

Armagnac-Ténarèze; Millésime, Single Cask, Cask Strength
tasting_notes: Blend of 65% Ugni Blanc and 35% Colombard. An exceptionally hot summer that year favored optimal grape maturity, giving rich, powerful and intense notes with remarkable aromatic depth.
Full-bodied and vibrant, with notes of stewed fruit and fruit compote, marrying quince, fig and dried apricot, and a good helping of oak on the finish.
Powerful nose of spiced butter, dried fruit, walnut, prune and vanilla; direct, balanced palate with rich, elegant tannins; long, refined, fresh finish.

Kirsch, cherry, stewed plum and cider apple with floral violet, clove, nutmeg, hazelnut and freshly sawn cedar; slightly sweet, fruity palate of prunes and dried fruit with drying oak tannins, tobacco, vanilla, quince and kirsch.

special_designation: Armagnac; Millésime; Millesime Collection Grand Armagnac
tasting_notes: Deep amber with golden highlights; aromas of ripe fruit including plum and apricot enriched by vanilla and toasted wood.
Pale yellow with golden highlights; fresh, precise nose dominated by fruit; soft attack with slight toasted notes and white-fruit aromas; smooth vanilla finish.
Supple and full-fruited with a rich smoky bouquet reminiscent of prunes and a lingering mellow finish.
Complex, virile and long-lived; elegant and refined on the palate, with a subtle smoky bouquet hinting of prunes and hazelnuts and a smooth lasting finish.

Delicate, spicy aromas of apricot, caramel, vanilla, orange peel, cinnamon and caramelised fruits; smooth, rich, full-bodied, fresh and fruity palate with a hint of ginger; rich finish with sweet spices and vanilla.
Copper colour with amber highlights; candied fruit, spices and noble rancio on the nose; soft palate with smooth notes of prunes, liquorice and cocoa.
Blend of 20 and 30 year olds; walnuts, coffee, prunes and ginger.
Average age around 10 years; vanilla with hints of coconut and marked fruity freshness on the palate.

special_designation: Armagnac-Ténarèze; Vieille Réserve; La Réserve de Gaston
tasting_notes: Golden mahogany; blend of 20-year Ugni Blanc and 10-year Folle Blanche; powerful woody nose with peach and mirabelle plum and noble spices; warm, sweet, full palate with a slightly salty note and very long finish.
100% Folle Blanche, matured two years in vat; powerful fruity nose of ripe pear, peach and banana with rosemary, floral when warmed; clean palate with violets and fresh cherries.
Nose of candied oranges and quince paste with slightly toasted wood; palate of citrus and fruit notes.
Orange-golden hue; candied orange and vanilla on the nose; long, smooth palate with mellow woodiness.
Deep orange hue. Nose: ripe black plum and fig. Palate: sweet with notes of mandarin and lightly roasted vanilla. Silver Medal, 2006 San Francisco World Spirits Competition.

tasting_notes: Aromas of pastry, almond paste and baking spice; viscous texture; spicy and peppery at the edges; seamless mineral finish. Bouquet of vanilla and plum with a touch of oaky rancio. No additive, no reduction, no filtration.

tasting_notes: Top-of-range estate single-cask millesime (700 EUR+ at the domaine shop); single vintage distilled and aged entirely at the chateau.

The original Fine Blanche, created 1985 by Patrick de Montal; unaged eau-de-vie aerated off the still and matured ~18 months, alcohol gradually reduced from 54% to 45%. Harvest and distillation dates inscribed on each bottle. Fruity and floral.
Earlier vintage of Arton's flagship unaged Fine Blanche (50cl), distilled at the estate and bottled without wood ageing at 45%.

White eau-de-vie off the alambic at 58%, rested in stainless steel min. 3 months, reduced to 43.2% with demineralized water. Nose of pear, apple, white blossom; ample creamy palate, sweet-almond finish. Silver, Talents de l'Armagnac 2019.
Estate Blanche d'Armagnac distilled on Ognoas's 1804 alambic (oldest working still in Gascony); sold individually and within the estate's Coffret Decouverte alongside the VSOP 6yo and XO 10yo.

Unaged white from the Jean Cave house; clear and transparent, very fresh floral/fruity nose, mineral attack with white-fleshed fruits, spicy finish. Retailer lists 43% (house also references a 40% version).

Blanche d'Armagnac from Veuve Lafontan, distilled at Cazaubon (Gers); transparent robe, light very floral nose, fresh attack with floral finesse, light finish. Stored in inert container, not oak-aged.

special_designation: Blanche Armagnac; Folle Blanche, Single Cask
tasting_notes: Unaged single-distillation white from Folle Blanche wine, 40% ABV; fragrant grape, ripe pear and pear-skin nose with oily/waxy notes, white-pepper finish. Silver, IWSC 2011. Marketed as a wine 'wodka' from Armagnac.
Unaged Blanche Armagnac from ODVI at 45%; fresh, fruity character with soft stone-fruit notes. (ODVI is a small Bas-Armagnac grower/brand; precise commune not disclosed on retailer listing.)

Single-variety unaged Blanche at 49%; very fruity (grapefruit, plum, fresh grape) and spicy (Sichuan pepper) nose. Folle Blanche is the historical Armagnac variety. NOTE: Darroze is a negociant/eleveur (sources ~30 estates), not a single own-make estate.

Single-variety unaged Blanche at 49% from Baco (a variety usually reserved for aging). Intense nose of mirabelle plum, white peach, fresh grape plus fennel and mint; supple dry palate, peppery finish. NOTE: Darroze is a negociant/eleveur, not a single own-make estate.

Single-variety unaged Blanche at 49% from Ugni Blanc; sharp, smooth, delicate medium-intensity nose of grape, plum, quince with fresh cane and cane sugar; silky palate, bitter-almond and vine-flower finish. NOTE: Darroze is a negociant/eleveur, not a single own-make estate.
Predominantly fruity - prunes, candied orange zest, quince; little wood influence; smooth and enveloping.
Fruit accompanied by first ageing aromas - soft spices, liquorice, cinnamon; still fiery, opens with air.
Full of life; tamed alcohol, refined tannins, aromas taking shape; prime drinking age.
Maturity - dried and candied fruit, assertive spice, first rancio, mellow alcohol; magnificent balance.
Style fully apparent; quality oak brings complexity and finesse.
Very old eaux-de-vie character - chocolate, leather, roasted notes; the age of reason.
Eternal; long delicate selection of armagnacs that travelled through time without a wrinkle.
Nose intensely fruity-spicy - ripe apricot and peach, vanilla, light wood; palate sweet and powerful, dried fruit, tobacco, citrus; long nutty finish.
Roast walnuts, apricots, prunes, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, toasted oak.
Elegant, distinguished, pre-phylloxera style; balance of power and elegance.
